title: Writing Parsers
summary: Turning text into data structures by hand - a tokenizer over chars with Peekable, tokens as an enum with positions, a recursive-descent parser that follows a small grammar, operator precedence, good error messages with the column of the problem, and a look at parser libraries such as nom.

cards.a:
`expr` calls `term` for its parts, so multiplications are grouped first

The nesting of the functions is the precedence: each part of a sum is a whole product. Grouping from the left comes from the loop in `expr`.

cards.q: Why keep the position of each token?
cards.a:
So error messages can say where the problem is

With positions, an error can point at the column, which helps users more than anything else a parser does.

cards.q: In recursive descent, how does a grammar rule become code?
cards.a:
as a function that calls the functions of the rules it uses

Each rule is a function; using another rule means calling its function, so nesting in the grammar becomes recursion.
